technical_distinctions.mechanism: Equal virtual addresses in different processes can map to different physical memory; mappings enforce protection and enable sharing.

technical_distinctions.mechanism: Reserved address space, committed memory, resident pages and swap backing are different quantities. Memory pressure can induce reclaim and page-fault thrashing.
technical_distinctions.discriminating_observation: Is the failure a virtual allocation limit, physical memory exhaustion or excessive page-in/page-out?

technical_distinctions.mechanism: Read-only mappings, shared memory and copy-on-write change which writes are visible across processes; the correct mechanism depends on ownership and synchronization.

technical_distinctions.mechanism: A race is dependence on event order; a data race is unsynchronized conflicting access under a given memory model. A system can have logically incorrect races even with no data race.
technical_distinctions.discriminating_observation: Which interleaving violates an application invariant?

technical_distinctions.mechanism: Deadlock has blocked cyclic dependency, livelock continues activity without useful progress, and starvation denies a runnable participant adequate service.
technical_distinctions.discriminating_observation: Is there a wait-for cycle, futile retry or unfair selection?

technical_distinctions.mechanism: A lock protects shared-state invariants; message passing transfers responsibility through a protocol. Neither automatically guarantees liveness or correct ordering.
technical_distinctions.discriminating_observation: What ownership model eliminates the disputed shared mutation?

technical_distinctions.mechanism: The write interface may acknowledge cached bytes before the device commits them. Durability needs an explicitly defined synchronization and storage contract.
technical_distinctions.discriminating_observation: What exactly survives power removal immediately after the acknowledged operation?

technical_distinctions.mechanism: An individually atomic update does not prove a multi-step filesystem operation survives a torn sequence. Journaling, copy-on-write and careful ordering preserve different invariants.
technical_distinctions.discriminating_observation: Which crash point can leave directory metadata or file contents inconsistent?

technical_distinctions.mechanism: Restarting a service does not imply preserved work; useful recovery needs durable checkpoints, idempotent operations or reconstruction from a log.
technical_distinctions.discriminating_observation: After restart, which application-level invariant is still true?

technical_distinctions.mechanism: Polling checks device readiness, interrupts signal events, and DMA transfers buffers with less CPU copying; each has separate scheduling and coherency implications.

technical_distinctions.mechanism: An interrupt merely signals a condition; a driver still must interpret status, obey ordering, handle timeouts and recover from unexpected hardware behavior.

technical_distinctions.mechanism: For controllers and robots, worst-case response time and safe fallback can matter more than aggregate operations per second.
technical_distinctions.discriminating_observation: Can the system guarantee its actuator remains safe when its scheduling deadline is missed?

technical_distinctions.mechanism: A remote display does not transfer the running process to the client. Browser/tab, transport, login session, process and file state have separate owners.

technical_distinctions.mechanism: A missing reply cannot distinguish an unexecuted remote operation from an executed operation whose response was lost; retries can duplicate effects.

entries.question: How does an operating system contain a stalled program?
aliases: Why does one frozen app not always freeze the whole computer?
entries.context: Distinguish a blocked process from global liveness loss.

entries.question: Why can a fully utilized CPU make little useful progress?
aliases: Why is the computer busy even when nothing useful gets done?
entries.context: CPU utilization is not a correctness or progress metric.

entries.question: How does an OS manage memory pressure?
aliases: Why does running out of memory slow everything down or kill one app?
entries.context: Differentiate address-space mappings, reclaim and process quotas.

entries.question: How can processes have independent views of the same virtual address?
aliases: How can two programs use the same memory address without colliding?
entries.context: Numeric addresses acquire meaning through their process mapping.

entries.question: How does an OS enforce access to devices, files and other processes?
aliases: Why can an app read one thing but not a camera, another app or a remote service?
entries.context: Find the responsible authorization mechanism rather than treating permission as universal.

entries.question: Why do device drivers and I/O failures affect system progress?
aliases: Why does plugging in a device sometimes need a driver or cause a freeze?
entries.context: Hardware events, driver code and scheduling interact.

entries.question: When does a successful file write become durable?
aliases: Why can a file be lost even though I pressed Save?
entries.context: A successful write may not be a durable commit.

entries.question: How can an OS recover consistently after a crash?
aliases: What must a computer do to recover safely after a crash?
entries.context: Correct recovery preserves invariants and progress, not merely rebootability.

entries.question: What keeps remote applications alive after a client disconnects?
aliases: Why can I disconnect from a computer and find my programs still running?
entries.context: A client connection can disappear without ending the server-side process.

entries.question: What survives closing an application, logging out or rebooting?
aliases: What is the difference between closing a window, logging out and restarting?
entries.context: Identify which state owner each action destroys.

entries.question: How does a computer bootstrap an operating system?
aliases: How does a computer get from turning on to running my own code?
entries.context: Identify firmware, loader, privileged runtime and their handoff contracts.

entries.question: How can an operating environment be built around a browser or a dedicated device?
aliases: Could I make a browser, console or robot into the computer's entire interface?
entries.context: Separate what users experience from what trusted system services supply.

entries.question: What is the smallest useful operating system we can build from existing components?
aliases: What is the smallest useful OS I could build without reinventing everything?
entries.context: Choose the minimal capability set and identify reusable infrastructure.

entries.question: How can distributed resources appear as one computing environment?
aliases: Can several computers behave like one coherent system?
entries.context: Shared experience does not imply shared failure, identity or consistency guarantees.

entries.question: How should a device-control system handle software stalls?
aliases: What should happen when software controlling a real device gets stuck?
entries.context: Physical deadlines and safe failure states can matter more than general-purpose throughput.

entries.question: How can we translate virtual addresses and check page permissions?
aliases: Can you translate a virtual address through page-table entries and determine access permissions?
entries.success_criterion: Given a page-table layout and access type, compute the physical address or appropriate fault; verify index and permission checks.

entries.question: How can we trace round-robin scheduling and calculate its latency?
aliases: Can you trace a round-robin scheduler and calculate waiting and response times?
entries.success_criterion: Given arrival times, time quantum and process bursts, derive the execution timeline and verify waiting and response metrics.

navigation_bridges.question: Which part of the system is still making progress?

choices.label: A program is blocked, spinning, or starved
choices.distinguishing_question: Can the kernel still schedule other work, and what is the blocked task waiting for?
choices.why: An unresponsive window can coexist with a healthy scheduler. CPU saturation, sleeping on I/O and starvation require different observations.

choices.label: Devices or memory pressure stall the whole system
choices.technical_title: Page faults, reclaim, interrupt and device paths
choices.distinguishing_question: Is time being spent reclaiming memory, faulting pages, or servicing a device?
choices.why: A fast CPU cannot hide a bottleneck that forces most progress to wait on memory or device completion.

navigation_bridges.question: Which resource or address-space contract failed?

choices.label: Addresses appear identical across processes
choices.distinguishing_question: Do equal virtual addresses resolve to the same physical page or two different mappings?
choices.why: An address is meaningful only relative to its address-space mapping; equality of numeric addresses does not imply aliasing.

choices.label: Memory is exhausted or slow
choices.distinguishing_question: Is failure caused by virtual-space limits, resident-memory pressure, reclaim, or explicit process quotas?
choices.why: Allocated, mapped, committed and resident bytes are not interchangeable. Repeated page faults can dominate elapsed time.

choices.label: A write returned but the machine lost power
choices.distinguishing_question: Did the write reach a durable medium, or only the OS or device cache?
choices.why: A successful write call may establish availability in a cache without guaranteeing survival of sudden power loss.

choices.label: After reboot, a file is partially updated or missing
choices.distinguishing_question: Was the data written atomically, ordered, journaled or recoverable after a torn update?
choices.why: Protecting individual writes is different from preserving filesystem-wide invariants through a crash.

choices.label: Closing a window or disconnecting a client
choices.technical_title: Display, connection, session and process lifetime
choices.distinguishing_question: Did the application process exit, the login session end, or only its presentation transport disconnect?
choices.why: The visible client is not necessarily the owner of the running application, and remote display transport can disappear while computation continues.

choices.label: Logging out, killing a process or restarting
choices.distinguishing_question: Which state lives only in memory, which belongs to an authenticated session, and which is stored persistently?
choices.why: A session teardown may terminate processes without affecting saved files; a machine restart removes volatile state even when durable profiles remain.

navigation_bridges.question: Where is the actual trust or ownership boundary?

choices.label: An app cannot access memory or a device
choices.technical_title: Address spaces, privilege modes, mediated I/O
choices.distinguishing_question: Is access blocked by page permissions, process credentials, device driver policy or application sandbox?
choices.why: Isolation and authorization are implemented at multiple layers; kernel privilege by itself does not explain who is allowed to use a camera or file.

choices.label: A request fails across computers
choices.technical_title: Remote identity, authentication and failure boundaries
choices.distinguishing_question: Who authenticates the requester and where is the authority for the resource located?
choices.why: Local permissions do not automatically grant remote access; the other machine has its own identities, policies and failure modes.

navigation_bridges.question: Which computing experience do I actually need to own?

choices.label: I want a new interface or application environment
choices.technical_title: Kernel contract versus shell and application platform
choices.distinguishing_question: Can an existing kernel and drivers already provide the safety, storage and device services needed?
choices.why: Replacing the user experience is often possible without rewriting the kernel; the motivation determines the minimal useful system boundary.

choices.label: I need unusual timing, devices or isolation
choices.distinguishing_question: Which hardware guarantees, latency constraints and fault models cannot be satisfied by reused components?
choices.why: A single-function device may simplify process and storage requirements while making deadlines and physical recovery more stringent.

navigation_bridges.question: What actually prevents concurrent work from finishing?

choices.label: Tasks interleave and corrupt shared state
choices.distinguishing_question: Which shared invariant becomes false under a particular interleaving?
choices.why: Mutual exclusion protects a critical invariant, not arbitrary application correctness. A reproducible interleaving reveals the missing synchronization.

choices.label: Tasks wait forever or starve
choices.distinguishing_question: Is there a cycle of dependencies, repeated unproductive retry, or systematic unfairness?
choices.why: Deadlock, livelock and starvation can all look like a freeze but require different interventions.

navigation_bridges.question: Where is shared state actually located?

choices.label: Two machines share a user experience
choices.technical_title: Remote execution, identity and session transport
choices.distinguishing_question: Is the application running here or elsewhere, and what remains alive if the connection drops?
choices.why: A remote screen can look local without sharing its process, filesystem or failure domain.

choices.label: Several machines cooperate on one result
choices.distinguishing_question: How do retries, duplicated requests and inconsistent views of state affect correctness?
choices.why: A crashed remote task and a lost reply are observationally similar; retrying without idempotency can execute an operation twice.

question_nodes.question: What stays alive when I close a window, disconnect, log out, or restart?
question_nodes.why_ask: An app window, a network connection, a login session, a running process, and saved state have different lifetimes. Which event actually ended the work?

question_nodes.question: Why can my computer be busy but make no useful progress?
question_nodes.why_ask: High CPU usage can mean productive work, spinning, contention, reclaim, interrupt load or stalled progress. Which measurable resource is limiting the task?

question_nodes.question: Why can one program run out of memory while another still works?
question_nodes.why_ask: Virtual addresses, physical pages, allocation limits, swapping and out-of-memory policy are different resources and boundaries.

question_nodes.question: Could a browser, robot, or game console be my whole operating environment?
question_nodes.why_ask: The experience someone uses can differ radically even when a familiar kernel, embedded runtime or remote machine supplies most system services.

question_nodes.question: Can a broken component recover without restarting the whole computer?
question_nodes.why_ask: Fault containment, restart supervision, persistent state and safe recovery are distinct contracts; surviving a crash is not the same as resuming correctly.

question_nodes.question: Why can an app access a file but not a camera, another app, or a remote service?
question_nodes.why_ask: Filesystems, process privileges, device mediation and remote authorization enforce different access boundaries; a single notion of 'permission' hides the mechanism.

question_connections.why: Running arbitrary programs introduces trust and privilege questions
Concurrent programs interact through address spaces and shared state
A restart is often where mistaken persistence assumptions become visible
Alternative architectures can change what 'building an OS' means
Boot and device interaction both depend on the target machine's contracts
What counts as a useful OS depends on why the user wants one
A different user experience may not require a new kernel
A device with trusted programs may need different protection guarantees
What one person can build depends strongly on which components are reused
A session can end while persistent data survives, or remain alive while unsaved data is lost.
CPU occupancy does not imply progress when tasks are contending or spinning.
Virtual isolation does not make physical memory infinite.
A distinct operating experience may be built above a reused kernel.
Recovery must be demonstrated after fault and restart, not inferred from successful initialization.
Resource-specific authorization is not equivalent to a single all-or-nothing kernel boundary.

source_inspected_observations.location: Preface > About This Book / Organization of This Book
source_inspected_observations.observation: The author describes the book as bare-metal firmware engineering, explicitly distinguishing it from an embedded-OS manual. The preface organizes the book as fourteen capability chapters, including architecture, hardware bring-up, interrupts, activity control, peripherals, debugging, connected devices, optimization, numeric techniques, power and motors.
source_inspected_observations.consequence: Read it to understand which tasks software performs without a kernel and which OS facilities may or may not earn their overhead.

source_inspected_observations.location: Chapter 5 — Interrupts; interrupt latency versus system latency
source_inspected_observations.observation: The book distinguishes the processor's time from IRQ arrival to ISR start from a worst-case system response bound affected by periods when interrupts are disabled. Interrupt handling and saved context consume cycles, and long handlers increase latency.
source_inspected_observations.consequence: An interrupt handler existing does not establish a real-time response guarantee; identify worst-case blocking and execution delays.

source_inspected_observations.location: Preface and Chapter 2, instruction set terminology (LEGv8 versus ARMv8)
source_inspected_observations.observation: The authors introduce LEGv8 as a deliberately restricted pedagogical subset based on ARMv8 and explicitly distinguish its instruction set from real ARMv8.
source_inspected_observations.consequence: Do not implement or debug real ARM exception/translation behavior from LEGv8 exercises alone; consult the actual architecture reference and target processor manuals.

source_inspected_observations.location: Further Reading > Chapter 5; references to The RISC-V Instruction Set Manual Volume II: Privileged Architecture
source_inspected_observations.observation: The architecture book itself directs readers to the privileged architecture manual for layered privilege modes, translation and protection details beyond the introductory Chapter 5 presentation.
source_inspected_observations.consequence: Use the architecture book to understand the physical contract, but use privileged ISA specifications for an implementable supervisor trap or page-table design.

cross_book_factors.question: Which OS functions genuinely need a privileged kernel?
cross_book_factors.mechanism: A superloop, finite-state machine, IRQ handlers and peripheral drivers can run directly on hardware; adding multiple independently untrusted programs changes isolation, resource arbitration and recovery requirements.
cross_book_factors.discriminator: Try satisfying the actual device requirement bare-metal; identify the first unmet contract that justifies a scheduler, protection domain, or service boundary.

cross_book_factors.question: How does a physical event become safe software action?
cross_book_factors.mechanism: Hardware raises an event, the processor takes an exception/interrupt path, low-level code saves state and acknowledges it, and deferred work or a main loop completes the operation under timing and concurrency constraints.
cross_book_factors.discriminator: Measure worst-case IRQ-to-useful-response latency, including masking, handler time and deferred work; compare polling and interrupts.

cross_book_factors.question: What lies beneath a process address and a memory fault?
cross_book_factors.mechanism: The instruction set produces virtual addresses; translations and permissions affect access; caches and coherence determine performance/visibility, while the OS supplies mappings, allocation, page-fault and reclaim policies.
cross_book_factors.discriminator: Differentiate translation/permission faults, physical memory pressure, cache misses and shared-memory ordering with their own measurements.

cross_book_factors.question: What turns source code into control of a real device?
cross_book_factors.mechanism: Compiler, assembler and linker produce an executable image; the processor executes instructions through an implementation, but firmware reset/boot handoff and board-specific peripheral setup remain platform contracts.
cross_book_factors.discriminator: Separate a hosted program startup example from reset vector, linker mapping, initialization, trap vector and actual bootloader responsibility.

cross_book_factors.question: How do multiple cores share memory without silently corrupting progress?
cross_book_factors.mechanism: ISA synchronization primitives, memory hierarchy/cache coherence and OS thread synchronization solve different pieces of the shared-memory problem. Coherence does not automatically provide atomicity for an application invariant.
cross_book_factors.discriminator: Construct a concurrent operation with well-defined ownership and measure whether the invariant survives interleavings and stalls.

cross_book_factors.question: What makes a useful physical computer persist beyond a successful demo?
cross_book_factors.mechanism: The device must bound memory, power, response times, peripheral errors, firmware update and recovery procedures; the OS may simplify services but does not by itself prove a safe physical session.
cross_book_factors.discriminator: Exercise representative faults, resets, power limits and updates; check that controlled hardware reaches safe states and correctly recovers.
